g.text: Provisional peer — planned, not yet carrying traffic

svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
# Reference set for genre `topology` (EXPERIMENTAL). figdown 0.1 topology title "Reference: topology fabric"
class uplink "Fabric uplink" stroke=#2563eb
group spine "Spine" node s1 "S1" shape=rounded in=spine node s2 "S2" shape=rounded in=spine
group leaf "Leaf" node l1 "L1" in=leaf node l2 "L2" in=leaf
external wan "WAN"
flow down rank s1,s2 rank l1,l2
edge s1 [e0/1] -- [e0/1] l1 class=uplink edge s1 [e0/2] -- [e0/1] l2 edge s2 [e0/1] -- [e0/2] l1 edge s2 [e0/2] -- [e0/2] l2 edge l1 -> wan edge l1 -- l2
# A SINGLE-MEMBER bundle (backlog 53). It is legal and it means # something real — a one-link LAG, an Ethernet Segment with one member — so the # declaration stands. What changed is the DRAWING: a ring exists to unite lines, # and around one line it unites nothing, so a one-member bundle now draws its # CAPTION beside the link and no ellipse. bundle mh "multi-home" l1--l2 # The MULTI-MEMBER form: the member list is ONE comma-delimited token, and each # member must resolve to a unique edge, as written (`s1--l1` is not `l1--s1`). # It was demonstrated in block-experimental.fd until 0.3, when `SCENE-KEYWORD-MEMBERSHIP` # withdrew `bundle` from `block`; `topology` is now its only genre, so the form # is demonstrated here. `topology` is also where the word can be defined by its # REFERENT — an IEEE 802.1AX LAG, an ECMP set, an EVPN Ethernet Segment — which # is what L1's two spine uplinks are. bundle ecmp "ECMP uplink set" s1--l1,s2--l1 # The WRITTEN-EMPTY label (`EMPTY-LABEL-STATE`): absent is omitted, `""` is a written value — # a third state, and the ring drew with no caption rather than falling back to # the id. This form was demonstrated on a `block` bundle until 0.3; it # moved here with the keyword, because `topology` is the only genre that # declares it now. # # THIS DECLARATION IS NOW MODEL-ONLY, AND DELIBERATELY KEPT ( # backlog 53). It is a SINGLE-member bundle, so it draws no ring, and its label # is written-empty, so it draws no caption: the figure shows nothing for it. # The line is not deleted, because it is the DEMONSTRATOR for the written-empty # label on `bundle` — the model still carries the trunk, `read` still reports # it, and a reader who asks the source what s2--l2 is gets an answer. Nothing a # ring around one unnamed line could draw is a fact the figure did not already # state, which is precisely why it now draws nothing. bundle unlabelled "" s2--l2
# WITHDRAWN — `plane tunnels "VXLAN overlay" z-index=1` stood here. `plane`, its # `z-index=` and the `plane=` that referenced one left the LANGUAGE # (`PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`), with no replacement spelling. Of the four scene genres this one had the # worst collision: in networking a plane is the control/data/management partition # of a device, and `topology` is the genre network engineers author in — so the # line above read as an architectural claim and in fact set a paint order. # A layering relation, if it ever earns a keyword, has a reserved word waiting: # `network` (RFC 8345 §4.1/§6.1). Today the one figure that wanted it is served # by `class` (`RESERVED-SPELLINGS`).
# The peer group earns its place in the subject (maintainer review, # 0.4): it is the spine's eBGP peering, reached by one real edge, so # the figure reads as one network rather than a catalogue with a loose corner. # It still carries its three demonstrators: `gap=` on the group, a node whose # dashed look is now a CLASSED meaning rather than bare presentation, and a # direct stroke= on the node showing the per-node override beside the class. class prov "Provisional peer — planned, not yet carrying traffic" style=dashed group peer "eBGP peers" gap=4 node p1 "Peer 1" in=peer class=prov stroke=#64748b node p2 "Peer 2" in=peer edge s2 -[eBGP]- p1
layout pin s1 at=(80,40) width=72 height=40 pin s2 at=(220,40) width=72 height=40
